title: Luke Burgis interviews Patrick Collison on aesthetics - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: A shownotes recap of Luke Burgis interviewing Patrick Collison on 'New Aesthetics,' arguing culture is stuck, that Silicon Valley has produced little art despite 50 years of wealth, and that a lost sense of the sacred underlies both aesthetic and technological stagnation.

insights.claim: Collison argues culture is 'stuck,' noting a 1926 Bauhaus building could pass for a structure built last year.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Frames aesthetic stagnation as a century-long phenomenon, a companion thesis to the 'Great Stagnation' in productivity.
insights.quote: a 1926 Bauhaus building could pass for last year’s

insights.claim: Collison ties the post-1971 cultural malaise to the loss of the sacred, arguing 'we lost the sacred, so we can’t have nice things.'
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Offers a cultural-spiritual explanation for the 1971 inflection point often discussed in economic-stagnation debates.
insights.quote: we lost the sacred, so we can’t have nice things
insights.locator: Patrick’s alternative theory of WTF happened in 1971

insights.claim: Collison observes that Detroit built the DIA after roughly 25 years of wealth, whereas Silicon Valley has been rich for 50 years yet its art tour could be done in a coffee break.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: A pointed critique that tech wealth has not translated into lasting cultural or artistic patronage.
insights.quote: We could do the Silicon Valley art tour in a coffee break
insights.locator: Detroit was rich for ~25 years and built the DIA

insights.claim: When asked to name any work of art made with AI, the conference audience responded with silence.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: A marker that generative AI had not yet produced a culturally recognized artwork as of the talk.
insights.quote: ”Can anyone name a work of art made with AI?” Silence.
insights.locator: ”Can anyone name a work of art made with AI?”

insights.claim: The discussion invokes Solzhenitsyn's claim that goodness and truth can be faked but beauty 'bears within it its own verification,' and cites the tourist gap between Toledo, Spain and Toledo, Ohio as evidence beauty is objective.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Advances an argument for objective aesthetic value, relevant to debates over cultural investment and taste.
insights.quote: you can fake goodness and truth, but beauty “bears within it its own verification”
insights.locator: Solzhenitsyn: you can fake goodness and truth
